diagnostics.message: :resource.helm_release.karpenter: explicit depends_on of :module.karpenter is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:resource.null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class: explicit depends_on of :module.eks is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:resource.null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class: explicit depends_on of :module.karpenter is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:resource.null_resource.update_kubeconfig: explicit depends_on of :module.eks is redundant — already implied by attribute references

`aws_eks_addon.aws_ebs_csi_driver` operates on the EKS cluster created by `module.eks`, but its `cluster_name = var.cluster_name` references only a variable, so no dependency on `module.eks` is inferred. Ordering currently works only indirectly via `depends_on = [module.self_managed_node_group]`; if that node group dependency is removed or reordered, the addon could be created before (or refreshed against) a cluster that doesn't exist yet.

`aws_eks_addon.eks_pod_identity_agent` operates on the EKS cluster created by `module.eks`, but its `cluster_name = var.cluster_name` references only a variable, so no dependency on `module.eks` is inferred. Ordering currently works only indirectly via `depends_on = [module.self_managed_node_group]`; the addon could be planned/applied against a cluster that doesn't exist yet if that indirect chain changes.

`null_resource.delete_daemonset` removes the `aws-node` daemonset (disabling the AWS VPC CNI), while `null_resource.create_calico_installation` applies the Calico Installation that takes over pod networking. Both resources depend only on `null_resource.update_kubeconfig`, so Terraform may delete `aws-node` before Calico's Installation exists, leaving pods without pod networking. Calico's standard EKS install order requires deleting `aws-node` only after the Installation is applied. Since both are local-exec kubectl resources, no attribute reference can express this ordering.

`null_resource.update_kubeconfig` has an explicit `depends_on = [module.eks]`, but its local-exec command already references `module.eks.cluster_name`, which establishes the dependency on `module.eks` implicitly.

`helm_release.karpenter` has an explicit `depends_on` on `module.karpenter`, but its `values` already reference `module.karpenter.service_account` and `module.karpenter.queue_name`, which establishes the dependency on `module.karpenter` implicitly.

`null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class` has an explicit `depends_on` on `module.eks`, but its `triggers` already reference `module.eks.cluster_primary_security_group_id` and `module.eks.cluster_security_group_id`, which establish the dependency on `module.eks` implicitly.

`null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class` has an explicit `depends_on` entry on `module.karpenter.node_iam_role_arn`, but its `triggers` already reference `module.karpenter.node_iam_role_arn`, which establishes the dependency on `module.karpenter` implicitly.
